Elevated CRP and ESR confirm systemic inflammation; normal uric acid and lack of crystal-associated features argue against gout. Imaging shows inflammatory synovitis without erosions or enthesitis — consistent with early ReA, not PsA or AS (which would require chronic changes, dactylitis, nail disease, IBD, or sacroiliitis). Gonococcal arthritis is excluded by negative NAAT and absence of dermatitis/tenosynovitis. Septic arthritis is highly unlikely given subacute course, no fever, no leukocytosis, and strong alternative explanation. The clinical evolution — self-limited ankle followed by persistent knee involvement — aligns with the typical migratory, asymmetric pattern of ReA.

[EVIDENCE]  
• Positive *Chlamydia trachomatis* NAAT confirms triggering infection  
• Dysuria × 3 weeks and pyuria (12–16 WBC/hpf) support urethritis  
• Asymmetric oligoarthritis: right knee swelling/pain × 12 days  
• Prior self-limited left ankle monoarthritis × ~1 week  
• HLA-B27 positive  
• CRP elevated (42 mg/L) and ESR elevated (38 mm/h)  
• Normal serum uric acid (5.1 mg/dL) argues against gout  
• Right knee ultrasound shows inflammatory synovitis (effusion, synovial thickening, minimal vascularity) without erosions or enthesitis  
• *Neisseria gonorrhoeae* NAAT negative rules out gonococcal arthritis  
• Absence of conjunctivitis, uveitis, keratoderma blennorrhagica, balanitis, or nail pitting defines “incomplete” ReA  

[GAPS]  
• Synovial fluid analysis (cell count, culture, crystals) not performed — would help definitively exclude septic arthritis or crystal-induced arthritis  
• No history or evaluation for gastrointestinal infection (e.g., *Campylobacter*, *Salmonella*, *Shigella*, *Yersinia*) — though chlamydia is confirmed, other triggers could coexist or modify presentation  
• No ophthalmologic exam documented — conjunctivitis may be subtle or transient and missed clinically  
• No assessment of enthesitis (e.g., Achilles or plantar fascia tenderness) — though not required for ReA diagnosis, its presence would further support spondyloarthropathy  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Reactive Arthritis
